svg.title: Baseline fleet repository architecture
svg.desc: Why the original research monorepo was split into Baseline and five sovereign product repositories, what each repository owns, how Quest Contracts, Studio, Lab, and Runtime fit together, which immutable package and artifact contracts cross repositories, and how every repository ties back to Baseline through decisions, evidence, status, and discovery rather than source-code coupling.
svg.text: Why the repositories are separate—and how they tie back to Baseline
One durable hub for meaning and proof · five sovereign implementation authorities · explicit immutable seams
1 · Why the monorepo became a fleet

g.text: Product code shared paths, build props, local feeds, release scripts,
compose identities, and commit ceremony—so local success hid coupling.
AFTER · Baseline hub + independently usable add-ons
Each product builds, tests, releases, and can be removed without a sibling checkout.
Small code seams are exact packages; larger seams are hash-verified artifacts.
The stable answer to “where does it live, why is it shaped this way, and what proves it?”
corpus mirrors · Pages · living fleet status

svg.text: NOT A META-BUILD · NO PRODUCT SOURCE · NO DEPLOYMENT OR RUNTIME AUTHORITY

g.text: Start at Baseline instead of scanning
read-only HEAD · exact-HEAD CI · release/evidence metadata → Baseline
The licensed game edge, telemetry, HUD,
tests, and mod release cadence move together.
one creator → certified artifact → game vertical
These surfaces share the quest contract and
iteration loop—not platform hosting or telemetry.
shared spine used by Studio, Lab, and Runtime
practice, explain, inspect, capture, and prove
Services, deployment, operator UX, and the
roadmap evolve as one implementation program.
without coupling shipped products to it.
not product hosting and is not HEARTH.
optional lab; products never report to it

svg.text: Arrow direction is producer → consumer. Baseline observes all five; only Platform corpus is mirrored into its tree.

g.text: Small shared schemas/types cross as a package, never a ProjectReference.
Transport identity stays platform-owned; the mod consumes exact bytes.
Platform verifies the built release; it never rebuilds mod source.

g.aria-label: Quest Studio package and release asset flow
g.text: Studio code is packaged; Lab/Picker pages and zips are hash-locked assets.

g.aria-label: Platform corpus mirror flow to Baseline
g.text: Workbench/roadmap inputs gain provenance; authority stays in Platform.
Optional lab boundary; no source bind-mount, product reporting, or HEARTH.
exact NuGet package · tagged/revisioned artifact · manifest · byte count · SHA-256
pushed-SHA corpus mirror · repository identity · current-head CI · evidence link
sibling checkout reach-in · cross-repo ProjectReference · shared build props · local-path default
convenience code copy · Baseline meta-build · mirror treated as writable authority

svg.text: Baseline ties the fleet together semantically—with a canonical map, durable rationale, evidence, provenance, and public discovery—not by owning or compiling every product.
